title: Evaluator brief omits older evidence when its discovery time budget is spent, producing insufficient_evidence verdicts
outcome: An acceptance evaluator is not left judging criteria without the evidence that exists on the task merely because the brief's discovery read budget ran out; omitted evidence is either read, or the omission is made explicit and recoverable before a verdict is recorded.
acceptance: When the brief's discovery budget stops paging before all of a task's evidence is read, the evaluator is told exactly which records were omitted and has a supported way to read them before judging, or the brief reads all the evidence that a criterion's verdict depends on.

A behavioural test with a task whose evidence exceeds the first page shows that the evaluator can reach the older evidence, and that an insufficient_evidence verdict is not recorded solely because of the time-budget omission.
Greg's minimum-60 s rule for operation-aborting limits still holds: no issued read is aborted below 60 s.
